After breakfast at the hotel, meet your English-speaking guide at the appointed time to begin your tour of Medellín, often called the City of Eternal Spring.

You'll explore the capital of Antioquia, Colombia's second most prominent city. The tour includes the Museum of Antioquia and Botero Plaza, where you can see the artist's work, including his well-known sculptures.

You'll then see the Palace of Culture and Veracruz Church, both national monuments in Medellín.

The tour also takes you to Comuna 13. Just a few years ago it was considered one of the city's most dangerous districts. Today it draws some of Medellín's largest numbers of visitors and is known for its graffiti and street culture. The change in the neighbourhood's reputation is especially clear here.

From Comuna 13, continue to El Castillo Museum. Built in 1930, the building is known for its art collections and gardens.

After the tour, arrive at your 5★ hotel and relax.
A Gothic church and elevated metro tracks among the buildings of Medellín, Colombia
Medellín: a church beside the metro line with the city and mountains behind it
Medellín to Pereira, the Cocora Valley and Salento

After breakfast, meet your English-speaking guide in the hotel lobby at the appointed time. Transfer to the airport and fly to Pereira.

From Pereira, head to the Cocora Valley. It lies in the central range of the Colombian Andes and is a major natural landmark in both Colombia and its Coffee Region.

On the walk, you'll see Colombia's national tree, the wax palm. It can grow to around 70 metres tall and live for more than 200 years. The tall, slender palms rise from green hillsides, forming one of Colombia's most recognisable landscapes.

After the walk, you'll have a lunch typical of the Salento region. Then explore Salento itself and learn about its history.

A traditional Colombian lunch is included. After the tour, return to Armenia, check in at the hotel and stay overnight.
